battle.name: 第一次英緬戰爭
battle.theater: 上緬甸伊洛瓦底河中游
battle.brief: 一八二四至一八二六年，東印度公司以孟加拉、印度支那與阿蘭克三路出兵攻緬，以野砲為核心火力：孟加拉縱隊靠輕野砲連奪帕戈德角、破耶特吉大軍，印度支那縱隊沿海路北進，砲隊越隘口重組，最後逼出阿瓦的《楊達波條約》，英軍未入緬甸王都。

kit.name: 野砲
kit.history: 能拆成幾件馬車拉走的砲。它讓野戰第一次有了可以計算的砲火。

countries: 交戰方為英國東印度公司聯軍與緬甸雍籍牙（康東）王朝。公司一側由加爾各答的最高政府統籌，總督阿默斯特調孟加拉與印度支那兩支大軍：孟加拉縱隊由約翰·阿奇博爾德·坎貝爾爵士率領，自阿薩姆方向北上；印度支那縱隊由准將阿奇博爾德·坎貝爾率領，取道毛淡棉與丹老，經三佛塔山口向東北推進；另有一支由阿蘭克方向出發的第三縱隊，規模最小。英國倫敦的董事會只批准有限目標，公司卻自行撥款、徵召匠役與輜重，皇家海軍派巡防艦進入伊洛瓦底河，公司蒸汽船負責運兵與牽制緬軍。緬甸以阿瓦為中央，國王蒲甘坐鎮御前，野戰大軍由敏豪·摩訶班杜拉統率，王儲敏耶覺沙領先鋒犯入阿薩姆，瑞皆、實皆省督分掌西北與東南邊區。緬軍骨幹是法、義教官依歐式操典訓練的德明營，配土邦民兵、象兵與火槍隊；阿薩姆的阿洪王素巴、撫密各邦土司與克倫首領則向英方求援，或退入山中以游擊周旋。
countriesEn: The belligerents were the forces of the British East India Company and the Burmese Konbaung (Toungoo) dynasty. On the Company side the Supreme Government in Calcutta directed the campaign, with Governor-General Lord Amherst drawing on the armies of the Bengal and Madras presidencies: the Bengal column under Sir John Archibald Campbell advanced from Assam, the Madras column under Brigadier-General Archibald Campbell moved by way of Tavoy and Mergui and pushed north-east through the Three Pagodas Pass, and a third and smallest column operated out of Arakan. The Board of Control in London sanctioned only limited objectives, yet the Company financed the effort, hired craftsmen and baggage trains, the Royal Navy sent frigates into the Irrawaddy, and Company steamers carried troops and kept the river corridor open. On the Burmese side Ava remained the centre, with King Bagyidaw holding court and the field armies commanded by Mingyi Maha Bandula, while the Crown Prince Minye Kyawswa led the assault on Assam and the viceroys of Rakhine and Tenasserim guarded the north-western and south-eastern frontier districts. The core of the Burmese army was the tamein regiments drilled to European manuals by French and Italian instructors, supported by native levies, war elephants and matchlock musketeers. Meanwhile the Ahom king Sukaphaa of Assam, the Shan chiefs and the Karen leaders looked to the British for protection, or fell back to the hills to wage a war of harassment.
people: 關鍵人物分屬兩方。緬甸方面，敏豪·摩訶班杜拉是全軍主腦，他自一八二〇年代起主持北方戰線，屢次挫敗英軍前鋒，一八二五年又率大軍西征暹羅，使英方得以集中兵力；一八二六年一月他在楊達波以北受重創而退，至二月初因傷勢惡化死去，臨終仍拒絕交出城市與王都。國王蒲甘起初不應戰，經內廷商議始授權議和；王儲敏耶覺沙既是阿薩姆戰役的元凶，也是後來主持北方邊疆與暹羅戰線的人。英方主角是兩位坎貝爾：孟加拉那位以堅忍與持久著稱，直到一八三八年才受封曼斯菲爾勳爵；印度支那那位把沿海攻勢推至大光，卻在雨季與給養上屢受挫。總督阿默斯特力主懲罰性遠征，與倫敦及後任坎寧侯的政策相左，使戰爭在英國內部引起非議。參戰者還包括一八二三年出使阿瓦的伯尼中校、一八二六年在阿瓦簽訂商約的克勞福德，以及阿洪王素巴、撫密土司與克倫首領。
peopleEn: The decisive personalities are found on both sides. In Burma, Mingyi Maha Bandula was the brain of the whole war effort: he directed the northern front from the early 1820s, repeatedly checked the British advance, and in 1825 led a large army west into Siam, which allowed the British to concentrate their force. Severely wounded north of Yandabo in January 1826, he withdrew and died of his wounds in early February, refusing to surrender a city or the royal capital. King Bagyidaw at first refused to fight and only authorised negotiations after deliberation at court; the Crown Prince Minye Kyawswa had led the invasion of Assam and later handled the frontier and Siamese fronts. On the British side the two Campbells dominate the record. The Bengal commander, famed for endurance, was not raised to the Mansfield peerage until 1838; the Madras commander pushed the coastal offensive as far as Toungoo but was repeatedly frustrated by the monsoon and by supply problems. Governor-General Amherst pressed for a punitive expedition, a policy at odds both with London and with his successor Canning, so the war drew sharp criticism inside Britain. The cast of participants also includes Lieutenant-Colonel Burney, sent to Ava in 1823, John Crawfurd, who concluded the commercial convention at Ava in 1826, and Ahom king Sukaphaa together with the Shan chiefs and Karen headmen.
kits: 野砲在這場戰爭裡是決定勝負的技術核心，也是十六世紀以來『可計算砲火』這一概念的成熟形態。一五五〇年前後出現的野砲把砲身、炮架、炮車與前車分解成數件，用馬匹拖行，行軍途中不必拆裝，臨陣只需拉上前車、放平支撐即可開火；到十九世紀二十年代，這套形式已固定為輕野砲連：六磅與九磅前裝滑膛砲，砲身與前車分載，一門用兩匹或四匹馬拉，後方另有備件車與藥車。孟加拉縱隊配十二門，印度支那縱隊配三十門，全軍火砲逾二百門，並有騎砲兵與馬匹牽引，趕路與作戰用同一套馬。英軍的野砲不追求最大射程，而是跟著步兵線前進，在距敵四百至八百米處展開，以密集的圓彈與霰彈齊射打散密集隊形，掩護線形射擊的步兵；帕戈德角與耶特吉兩役，砲火正是擊潰緬軍縱隊的主要手段。緬軍也備有自鑄銅砲與數量有限的野砲，但多守於寨牆與城門之後，其軍隊真正的重火力仍在冷兵器與火槍。此外英軍還攜帶火箭連與隨艦火砲，蒸汽船可沿江襲擊，砲火與機動第一次在同一個戰場上結合。
kitsEn: The field gun stood at the technical heart of this war and was the mature form of a calculable artillery that had begun in the sixteenth century. The field gun of around 1550 broke the piece down into several loads — barrel, carriage, trail and limber — for draught horses to tow, so that it needed no assembly on the march and could be brought into action simply by drawing up the limber and dropping the trail. By the 1820s that idea had settled into the light field battery: six- and nine-pounder muzzle-loading smoothbores, barrel and limber carried separately, two or four horses to a gun, with a reserve wagon and an ammunition wagon behind. The Bengal column had twelve guns, the Madras column thirty, and more than two hundred pieces served with the army in all, with horse artillery teams for mobility. British field guns did not seek maximum range: they advanced with the infantry line, unlimbered at four to eight hundred metres, and poured massed salvos of round and grape shot into close formations, covering the linear volleys of the foot and breaking the momentum of Burmese columns. Pagoda Point and Ywetgyi were won in large measure by that artillery fire. The Burmese had their own cast bronze guns and a limited number of field pieces, but these were mostly emplaced behind stockades and gateways, and the real weight of Burmese striking power remained with cold steel and muskets. British rocket detachments and naval guns supplemented the field artillery, and steamers could work up and down the river, so that gunnery and mobility met for the first time on the same battlefield.
tactics: 英軍以三縱隊同步推進為骨架，以『砲隨步兵』為火力骨架。孟加拉縱隊越過帕特凱山口後沿伊洛瓦底河中游北行，先取帕戈德角，再在耶特吉迎擊摩訶班杜拉大軍；行軍時把野砲、藥箱、炊具與渡河器材分車載運，靠象群、牛車與河運維持一日行程，遇到緬軍據點則以輕野砲壓制，步兵結陣攻堅。印度支那縱隊沿毛淡棉—丹老走廊北進，越三佛塔山口，砲兵隊利用狹窄山道把野砲分件人力搬過隘口，再於大光附近重新組列砲隊。英軍戰術要點有三：以連續步兵齊射與野砲齊射交替，使衝鋒縱隊被整片火力壓住；用騎砲兵與遊騎繞擊側翼，逼退包圍；靠河流與海運維持糧彈，使遠征不必依賴陸路輜重。緬軍則發揮兵多、熟悉地形、擅長游擊與拖延的長處：面對英軍縱隊不正面接戰，而以大隊迂迴、夜襲與襲擾消耗英軍，必要時退入雨季與縱深，並以城寨與野地土壘遲滯英軍。其現代化德明營會用歐式線形射擊與刺刀衝鋒，但面對已完成射擊準備的英軍步兵與野砲，仍難以扭轉局勢。
tacticsEn: British operations were organised around three columns advancing in step, with the guns going with the infantry as the skeleton of its fire. The Bengal column crossed the Patkai passes and moved north along the middle Irrawaddy, taking Pagoda Point and then meeting Maha Bandula's army at Ywetgyi; on the march it carried guns, ammunition boxes, cooking kits and river-crossing equipment on separate wagons, sustaining one day's advance with elephants, bullock carts and river transport, and used light field guns to silence Burmese positions before infantry stormed the stockades. The Madras column advanced north along the Tavoy–Mergui corridor, crossed the Three Pagodas Pass, and had its artillery teams man-handle the guns piece by piece over the narrow mountain tracks before re-forming battery lines near Toungoo. Three features mark British tactics: continuous infantry volleys alternating with massed field-gun fire, so that a charging column was smothered; horse artillery and light cavalry sweeping the flanks to break encirclements; and a reliance on river and coastal shipping to feed the army, so that a distant expedition did not depend on overland baggage. The Burmese fought as the numerous, terrain-wise and harassment-minded force they were: they avoided set-piece collision with the advancing columns, striking with flanking bodies, night attacks and raids, falling back into the monsoon and the interior when pressed, and using stockades and field earthworks to slow the British. Their modernised tamein regiments could fire in European linear fashion and charge with the bayonet, but against infantry that had already completed its firing drills, backed by field guns, the balance of the encounter would not turn.
data: 兵力與編制方面，公司投入的野戰部隊通常被記為一萬三千人上下，火砲逾二百門；孟加拉縱隊約六千人、十二門砲，印度支那縱隊約九千人、三十門砲，阿蘭克方向的第三縱隊僅約兩千人。緬軍野戰兵力在高峰時遠高於此，摩訶班杜拉在北線曾集結二萬以上兵力，但因同時在西北、暹羅與內陸多線用兵，無法集中。距離上，仰光至阿瓦沿伊洛瓦底河約一千一百公里，楊達波在阿瓦以南不足五十公里；帕戈德角距阿薩姆邊境約三百公里。時間上，一八二四年二月宣戰，三月有帕戈德角與耶特吉兩戰，五月英軍進入仰光，一八二五年九月仰光談判破裂，同年十二月至一八二六年一月最後一輪進攻，二月二十四日簽訂楊達波條約。損失方面，英軍陣亡與負傷合計約一千五百人，其中因疾病與後勤造成的比例甚高，戰爭開支約五十萬英鎊；緬軍陣亡數以萬計，多散於襲擾與攻城戰，統計從缺。條約訂定緬甸分期支付五十萬盧比賠款。每門野砲需二至四匹馬、一門前車與數箱定裝藥，全軍的糧食與火藥靠河運與牛車分批輸送。
dataEn: On numbers, the Company is usually credited with about thirteen thousand men in the field and more than two hundred guns: roughly six thousand men and twelve guns in the Bengal column, about nine thousand men and thirty guns in the Madras column, and a third column of some two thousand men out of Arakan. Burmese field forces were at times far larger, Maha Bandula at one point massing upwards of twenty thousand in the north, but with forces committed simultaneously in the north-west, in Siam and in the interior they could never be concentrated. In distance, Rangoon to Ava is about eleven hundred kilometres by the Irrawaddy, and Yandabo lies less than fifty kilometres south of Ava; Pagoda Point is some three hundred kilometres from the Assam frontier. In time: war was declared in February 1824; Pagoda Point and Ywetgyi were fought in March; the British entered Rangoon in May; the Rangoon talks broke down in September 1825; the final advance ran from December 1825 into January 1826; and the Treaty of Yandabo was signed on 24 February 1826. In losses, British dead and wounded together came to roughly fifteen hundred, with disease and logistics accounting for a high share, and the war cost about half a million pounds sterling; Burmese dead numbered in the thousands, mostly in raids and sieges, and no complete count survives. The treaty fixed an indemnity of five hundred thousand rupees to be paid in instalments. Each field gun needed two to four horses, a limber and several boxes of fixed ammunition, and the army's food and powder moved in batches by river and bullock cart.
cause: 開戰緣於東印度公司與雍籍牙王朝在西北邊界的長期對撞。十八世紀末以來，緬甸不斷向北擴張，先後控制撫密諸邦，再於一八二一至一八二二年大舉犯入阿薩姆，攻破阿洪國的邊寨，逼近公司所保護的產區與哨站。公司的邊境委員會要求緬軍退兵、承認既有條約並歸還所掠物資，緬方始終不予答覆；一八二三年英方再派中校伯尼赴阿瓦交涉，得到的待遇近乎侮辱，談判數度破裂。公司於是先以海軍封鎖仰光、扣留緬方船隻，再於一八二四年二月宣戰。值得注意的是，倫敦方面只批准有限的懲罰性目標，總督阿默斯特卻推動不受節制的遠征，志在打通北線、迫阿瓦屈服，這使戰爭在初期就已超出政府設定的目的，也埋下日後英國政府反對攻入王都的分裂。
causeEn: The war grew out of the long collision between the East India Company and the Konbaung dynasty along the north-western frontier. Since the late eighteenth century Burma had pushed steadily north, first taking the Shan states, then invading Assam in 1821–1822, storming the Ahom frontier forts and closing on the districts and outposts the Company claimed to protect. The Company's frontier commissioners demanded that the Burmese withdraw, respect existing treaties and return what they had taken; the Burmese court gave no answer, and when the British sent Lieutenant-Colonel Burney to Ava in 1823 the envoy was treated with something close to contempt and the negotiations collapsed. The Company first closed Rangoon with the navy and detained Burmese shipping, and then declared war in February 1824. It is worth noting that London had approved only a limited punitive object, while Governor-General Amherst drove an expedition that was not to be restrained and aimed at breaking the northern line and humbling Ava. From the outset the war thus outran the purpose set by the government, and that division was to resurface when Britain called a halt before the capital could be stormed.
impact: 戰爭把雍籍牙王朝從上緬的強權推入依附英國的守勢。割地、賠款、常駐代表與商約四項一併加身，緬王雖保住阿瓦與其正統，卻失去阿薩姆、卡查爾與整個南部出海走廊，國防從山防線退化成仰光與丹老等幾個沿海據點。此後數十年裡，緬使團屢次赴印求援不得，反而屢遭英方提出新的邊界與商貿要求；大光趁勢坐大，取代阿瓦成為上緬的實際政治中心，阿瓦的國王成了大光與英方之間的中介。區域格局同樣被牽動：緬甸曾致書清朝求援而未獲回應；同年緬暹戰爭又牽走大批緬軍，成為英方得以取勝的關鍵變數。技術層面上，野砲的密集齊射、火箭與蒸汽船在同一戰役並用，顯示東印度公司已把砲兵、機動與後勤組成一套可重複的標準，這套經驗成為後來印度洋與印度大陸作戰的樣板，也把公司推向更積極的擴張，直接為一八五二與一八八五年兩次英緬戰爭埋下鋪墊。英國內部則出現反戰聲浪，阿默斯特的遠征政策被批為越權。
impactEn: The war pushed the Konbaung dynasty from the position of a great power in upper Burma into a dependent posture towards the British. Ceded territory, indemnity, a permanent resident and a commercial convention were imposed together. The king kept Ava and his own legitimacy, but lost Assam, Cachar and the entire southern outlet to the sea, and Burma's defence shrank from a line of mountain fortresses to a handful of coastal points, Rangoon and Tavoy among them. For decades afterwards Burmese missions to India asked for help and got none, and were met instead with fresh British demands about frontiers and trade; Toungoo rose to take Ava's place as the real political centre of upper Burma, leaving the Ava king as an intermediary between Toungoo and London. The regional balance shifted as well: Burma wrote to the Qing court for assistance and received no answer, and the Burmese–Siamese war of the same year drained away a large Burmese army and was the decisive variable that made the British victory possible. At the level of technique, massed field-gun fire, rockets and steamers were used together in one campaign for the first time, showing that the Company had assembled artillery, mobility and logistics into a repeatable standard; that experience became the template for later campaigning in the Indian Ocean and on the Indian mainland, and pushed the Company towards a more aggressive expansion, laying the ground for the Anglo-Burmese wars of 1852 and 1885. In Britain the war also raised an anti-war voice, and Amherst's overriding policy was attacked as an excess of authority.
result: 一八二六年二月二十四日，緬甸與公司在阿瓦以南的楊達波村簽訂條約，正式結束戰事。條約主要內容為：緬甸放棄阿薩姆、卡查爾與琴蒂亞地區，承認撫密諸邦及克倫地區的獨立並接受英方保護，不得再向西北擴張；割讓阿蘭克部分土地與毛淡棉、丹老、仰光及指定島嶼，並分期支付五十萬盧比賠款；接受英國在阿瓦派駐常駐代表，開放貿易，一八二六年由克勞福德另訂商約。英軍並未攻入阿瓦，楊達波成為曼德勒以北談判的極限；英國政府這時反而叫停進一步攻勢，避免把公司遠征升級為攻陷王都的全面戰爭。摩訶班杜拉死後，緬軍失去最能打仗的指揮官，元氣大傷，國王蒲甘把實權交給大光一系。結果是雙方實力差距被重新劃定：英國確立了在印度的北方屏障，緬甸保住生存卻失去南方與西部，約二十年的相對和平由此開始，直到一八八五年王都被攻陷，局面才被徹底改寫。
resultEn: On 24 February 1826 the Burmese and the Company signed the treaty at the village of Yandabo south of Ava, formally ending the war. Its main terms: Burma renounced Assam, Cachar and Jaintia, recognised the independence of the Shan states and of the Karen areas and accepted British protection over them, and undertook no further expansion to the north-west; it ceded part of Arakan together with Tavoy, Mergui, Rangoon and certain islands, and paid an indemnity of five hundred thousand rupees in instalments; it accepted a permanent British representative at Ava and opened trade, a separate commercial convention following with Crawfurd in 1826. The British did not enter Ava: Yandabo marked the limit of negotiation short of the capital, and the British government at this point called a halt rather than let a Company expedition escalate into a war to capture the royal city. With Maha Bandula dead, the Burmese lost their ablest commander and their fighting spirit with him, and the king transferred real power to the Toungoo party. The result was a redrawing of the balance of power: Britain established a northern shield for India, while Burma survived but lost the south and the west, and some twenty years of relative peace began, until the fall of Ava in 1885 rewrote the settlement completely.
